Monday to Friday, 9:00–15:00, at the cash office: help with your valuation notice and land rates.

Staff of the Revenue Department help you read your valuation notice, calculate your land rates and set up payment by mobile money.

Time: Monday to Friday, 9:00–15:00
Cost: Free
Registration: Not needed
Every evening from 16:00 to 22:00 at the jetty: food, crafts and music.

Food, crafts and music every evening before Christmas.

Time: Every evening, 16:00–22:00
Cost: Free entry
Registration: Traders apply for a stall at the Trade & Markets Office until 1 December
Municipal grounds, 9:00–14:00. Flag raising, speeches, school choirs and traditional dances.

The municipality celebrates Jamhuri Day with the flag raising, speeches, school choirs and traditional dances.

Time: 9:00–14:00
Cost: Free
Registration: Not needed
Mto Safi Polytechnic, 9:00–15:00. Bring copies of your CV and certificates.

Employers from tourism, fishing, construction and IT present jobs and apprenticeships. Bring copies of your CV and certificates.

Time: 9:00–15:00
Cost: Free
Registration: Recommended, at the Education Office
Municipal hall, 10:00. Every resident may speak.

Every resident may speak. The forum is held in Kiswahili and English. Sign language interpretation is available on request until 15 November.

Time: 10:00–13:00
Cost: Free
Registration: Not needed
Meet at the lifeguard tower on the public beach, 7:00. Gloves, bags and water provided.

Residents, schools and businesses clean the beach together. Gloves, bags and water are provided. The cleanest group wins a tree for its school.

Time: 7:00–11:00
Cost: Free
Registration: Not needed
Public beach, meeting point at the lifeguard tower
New fish market opens at the jetty
Sixty stalls, cold storage and clean water for traders and buyers.

The new fish market at the jetty opened on Monday. It has sixty stalls, a cold room for the night’s catch and running water at every stall.

Traders who sold at the old market keep their stall number. New traders apply for a stall at the trade office in the municipal office. The market opens daily from 5:00 to 18:00.

Contact: Trade & Markets Office, +254 700 000 010
Works run for six weeks. Matatus take the diversion via Market Street.

Beach Road between the roundabout and the public beach gets a new surface and drainage. The works start on 3 November and run for about six weeks.

During the works, matatus and lorries take the diversion via Market Street. Pedestrians and bicycles can pass at all times. Shops along Beach Road stay open.

Contact: Roads Department, +254 700 000 020
Eye tests, vaccinations and screening, open to every resident.

The municipality and the Ward 3 health centre hold a free health camp on 25 and 26 October at Ward 3 Primary School, from 8:00 to 16:00.

On offer: eye tests, blood pressure and diabetes screening, and vaccinations for children. Bring your health card if you have one. No appointment is needed.

Contact: Health Department, +254 700 000 030
Pay land rates by mobile money from January
Residents can now pay land rates and business permits with their phone.

From 1 January 2027, residents pay land rates, the single business permit and market fees by mobile money. The receipt arrives by SMS and counts as proof of payment.

Payment at the cash office in the municipal office stays possible. The land rates calculator on our website shows what you owe before you pay.

Contact: Revenue Department, +254 700 000 040
Have your say on the budget 2027/28
Public participation forums in every ward in November.

The municipality prepares its budget for 2027/28 and asks residents what matters most to them: roads, water, markets, health or schools.

A forum takes place in every ward in November. The main forum is on 22 November in the municipal hall. Residents who cannot attend send their views in writing to the municipal office by 30 November.

Contact: Planning Office, +254 700 000 050
Mto Safi named cleanest town on the coast
The monthly beach clean-ups and the new waste collection paid off.

Mto Safi has won this year’s Clean Coast Town Award. The jury praised the monthly beach clean-ups by residents and schools, and the new waste collection in all wards.

The mayor thanked every volunteer and announced that the clean-ups continue every third Saturday of the month.

Contact: Environment Department, +254 700 000 060
New boreholes bring clean water to Ward 5
Three boreholes and twelve water kiosks serve 4,000 residents.

Three new boreholes in Ward 5 now supply twelve water kiosks. About 4,000 residents no longer have to walk to the river for water.

A water kiosk is open from 6:00 to 19:00. A 20-litre container costs KES 5.

Contact: Water & Sanitation Department, +254 700 000 070

fieldlist.field: The municipality publishes every tender above KES 500,000 here and on the national procurement portal. Bids are submitted in a sealed envelope at the procurement office before the closing date.
Number|Subject|Closes MSM/T/01/2026|Resurfacing of Market Street|12 June MSM/T/02/2026|Solar street lights, Beach ward|19 June MSM/T/03/2026|Waste collection vehicles (2)|26 June
Ask for the information we hold

Every citizen has the right to the information the municipality holds. Ask for a document in writing, by email or at the front desk of the municipal office, and say as precisely as you can what you are looking for.

We answer within 21 days. Copies cost KES 10 per page; electronic copies are free.
The budget and the annual accounts The valuation roll The minutes of the municipal board Tenders and the contracts awarded

This is placeholder text for the demo site. The municipality writes its own privacy policy here: which personal data the site and its forms collect, what for, how long it is kept and whom visitors contact about it.

This is placeholder text for the demo site. The municipality writes its own accessibility statement here: the standard the site aims at, what is not accessible yet and how visitors report a barrier.

The design of this site targets WCAG 2.1 level AA.

In the e-services portal you pay land rates, permits and fees, apply for a water connection and download your receipts, at any time of day.

Log in with your eCitizen account. You do not have one yet? Register at eCitizen first; it takes five minutes.

fieldlist.field: Have your say on the budget

Before the county assembly decides on the budget, the municipality presents it in every ward. Come to a forum, ask questions and tell us what your ward needs most.

You can also send your views in writing to the clerk until 15 May.
Ward|Date|Place Central|4 May, 10:00|Municipal hall Beach|6 May, 10:00|Pwani primary school Upper River|8 May, 14:00|Kijiji social hall Mnarani|11 May, 10:00|Mnarani chief's camp

White beaches, a quiet river mouth and the old dhow harbour bring visitors to Mto Safi all year round. Tourism and the fish trade are what the town lives from.

The tourist information at the jetty helps with accommodation, boat trips and guides. Businesses that want to start here find the permits they need under Single business permit.

White beaches, a quiet river mouth and the old dhow harbour bring visitors to Mto Safi all year round. Tourism and the fish trade are what the town lives from.

The tourist information at the jetty helps with accommodation, boat trips and guides. Businesses that want to start here find the permits they need under Single business permit.

fieldlist.field: The dhow harbour and the fish market at sunrise The mangrove boardwalk at the river mouth Mto Safi beach and the coral garden The old town with its carved doors
Mto Safi means "clean river", and we work to keep it that way: with a sewage plant that serves the town centre, waste collection twice a week and clean-up days in every ward.

To connect a plot to the water supply, apply in the e-services portal with the plot number. A connection to a house on a plot along a main pipe costs KES 6,500 and takes about three weeks.

To report a leak or a burst pipe, call +254 700 000 001 at any time.
Town centre: Monday and Thursday Beach and Mnarani: Tuesday and Friday Upper River: Wednesday and Saturday

The municipality runs four health centres and eleven dispensaries. Maternal care, vaccinations and the treatment of common illnesses are free in all of them.

For an emergency, call 1199 or go to Mto Safi Sub-County Hospital, which is open day and night.
Health centre|Ward|Opening hours Mto Safi Town|Central|Mon–Sat 7:00–19:00 Pwani|Beach|Mon–Fri 8:00–17:00 Kijiji|Upper River|Mon–Fri 8:00–17:00 Mnarani|Mnarani|Mon–Fri 8:00–17:00
Pay the municipality from wherever you are

Land rates, permits, parking and market fees pay for the roads, the street lights, the markets and the waste collection of Mto Safi.

Most of them can be paid by mobile money or by card in the e-services portal, at any time of day. The cash office in the municipal office is open on working days.

Most of them can be paid by mobile money or by card in the e-services portal, at any time of day. The cash office in the municipal office is open on working days.

fieldlist.field: Interest waived when you clear your arrears

Owners who pay all their land rate arrears in one sum before 30 June can apply for a waiver of the interest on them.

Apply at the cash office or in the e-services portal before you pay. The waiver is granted once per plot.
Ask for a statement of your arrears Apply for the waiver with the statement Pay the arrears without the interest within 30 days of the approval

Mto Safi runs three markets: the central market on Market Street, the fish market at the jetty and the Saturday market at the bus park.

Traders with a stall pay a monthly fee, traders without one a daily fee at the gate. A free stall is allocated by the market office; ask there for the waiting list.
|Fee Stall, per month|KES 1,200 Open space, per day|KES 50 Fish market, per day|KES 80

Parking in the town centre and on Beach Road is paid from Monday to Saturday, 7:00 to 18:00. Sundays and public holidays are free.

Pay by mobile money with your number plate, or buy a monthly sticker in the e-services portal.
Vehicle|Per day|Per month Car|KES 100|KES 2,000 Pick-up and van|KES 150|KES 3,000 Lorry|KES 300|KES 6,000 Motorcycle (boda boda)|KES 30|KES 500

Every business in Mto Safi, from a kiosk to a hotel, needs a single business permit. It replaces the separate trade, health and fire licences, and it is valid for the calendar year.

Apply for a new permit or renew yours in the e-services portal. A renewal is due by 31 January.
Your national ID or passport The KRA PIN of the business The plot number of the premises A description of the activity and the number of employees
How your land rates are calculated

Every owner of land in Mto Safi pays land rates once a year. The rate is a share of the rateable value of your plot. The valuation roll sets that value, and your valuation notice states it. The share depends on what the land is used for.

Pay before 31 March. From April, interest of 1 % of the annual rate is added for every month the rate stays unpaid.
Land use|Rate|Minimum per plot and year Residential|0.5 % of the rateable value|KES 1,500 Commercial|1.2 % of the rateable value|KES 1,500 Agricultural|0.2 % of the rateable value|KES 1,500
Pay by mobile money, by card in the e-services portal, or at the cash office in the municipal office. Keep the receipt: it is your proof of payment.
